title: Which town has the most people, and how do you order all six?
description: Joseph reads six town populations on a district notice board. The video orders them from greatest to least, comparing from the left.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare the biggest place first, and look at the next place only when the digits match. Watch for picking a number because it has big digits in the lower places.

source: Let Us Do (second set) 5, population of towns
video_script.why: The child can order prices from least to greatest but has not yet ordered from greatest to least with matching leading digits.
video_script.substitution: Sort by the ten thousands digit, then compare the thousands inside the groups that match, and list from the greatest.
video_script.anchor: Joseph reading town populations on a district notice board
video_script.wrong_answer: town five has the greatest population, because it has the biggest digit, eight
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu picks Town five as the greatest because of the eight in its hundreds place. But the biggest place decides, and Town five has the smallest ten thousands digit.
video_script.payoff_line: the six towns are now in order from the greatest population to the least

final_answer.spoken: Town six with sixty-six thousand five hundred and forty, Town one with sixty-five thousand two hundred and thirty-two, Town three with fifty-six thousand three hundred and eighty, Town two with fifty-three thousand two hundred and thirty-one, Town four with fifty-one thousand three hundred and thirty-six and Town five with forty-five thousand eight hundred and fifty-eight

maths_rules: six towns: Town 1 65,232; Town 2 53,231; Town 3 56,380; Town 4 51,336; Town 5 45,858; Town 6 66,540; all have 5 digits
ten thousands digits: 6, 5, 5, 5, 4, 6; so the two with 6 come first, then the three with 5, then Town 5 with 4
Town 6 vs Town 1: thousands 6 and 5; 6 > 5, so 66,540 > 65,232
slip: Town 5 has 8 in the hundreds place, but its ten thousands digit 4 is the smallest, so 45,858 is the least
video_script.design: Exercise: order six five digit populations from the greatest. Hint: the ten thousands digit first. The six town rows stay on the stage and the sorted list is built below them.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a district notice board with six rows: Town 1 65,232, Town 2 53,231, Town 3 56,380, Town 4 51,336, Town 5 45,858, Town 6 66,540; an empty list of six boxes below

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='board'/>Joseph reads a notice board in the district office. It lists the people living in six towns.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Town one has sixty-five thousand, two hundred and thirty-two. Town two has fifty-three thousand, two hundred and thirty-one.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Town three has fifty-six thousand, three hundred and eighty. Town four has fifty-one thousand, three hundred and thirty-six.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Town five has forty-five thousand, eight hundred and fifty-eight. Town six has sixty-six thousand, five hundred and forty.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Put the towns in descending order, the greatest population first.

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

narration: <bookmark mark='look'/>Look at the ten thousands digit of each town first.
<bookmark mark='need'/>The greatest population has the biggest digit in the biggest place.
<bookmark mark='try'/>Which towns share the same digit there? Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows Town 5 first; the 8 in the hundreds place of 45,858 is circled; the ten thousands digit 4 glows; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.eight: the 8 in the hundreds place is circled

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Town five has the greatest population, because it has the biggest digit, eight.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>That eight sits in the hundreds place.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The ten thousands place is far more important, and Town five has only four there.

beats.on_screen: Town 6 and Town 1 are compared by thousands and placed in boxes one and two

marks.six: the ten thousands digits of Town 6 and Town 1 glow
marks.first: Town 6 and Town 1 move to boxes one and two

narration: <bookmark mark='six'/>Two towns have six in the ten thousands place, Town six and Town one.
<bookmark mark='th'/>Look at the thousands. Town six has six and Town one has five.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Town six is greater, then Town one.

beats.on_screen: Town 3, Town 2 and Town 4 are compared by thousands and placed in boxes three, four and five; Town 5 is placed in box six; the answer card shows the full list

marks.five: the thousands of the three towns glow

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Three towns have five in the ten thousands place. Their thousands are six, three and one.
<bookmark mark='order'/>Six is greatest, then three, then one. That puts Town three, Town two and Town four in a row.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Town five has four in that place, the least of all, so it comes last.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The six towns are now in order from the greatest population to the least.

<bookmark mark='rule'/>If the digits match, look at the next place to the right.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Does each town in your list have a smaller population than the one above?
